specification.problem: Quantum Viterbi algorithm (QVA): find the most probable path through a decoding trellis (hidden Markov model, e.g. convolutional code with constraint length Q and N decode frames) by building a superposition over all legal paths with phase depending on path probability given received data, then using specialized amplitude amplification so the most probable path is likely to be measured.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the QVA problem and key relations only; exact state-preparation circuits, oracle construction, and complexity bounds are not given in the abstract. Small finite trellis instance assumed for any illustration.

symbols.meaning: constraint length of the convolutional code (state-space size scale)
number of frames in the decode window (trellis length)
fanout: number of possible transitions from a given state in the hidden Markov model
symbols.domain: positive integer, generally much less than Q

symbols.meaning: a legal path through the decoding lattice
symbols.domain: sequence of N states consistent with trellis transitions

symbols.meaning: probability of path pi given received data r

equations.label: Path superposition with probability-dependent phase
equations.description: Uniform superposition over the set L of legal paths with phase a function of path probability.
equations.abstract_quote: The QVA constructs a superposition of states which correspond to all legal paths through the decoding lattice, with phase a function of the probability of the path being taken given received data.
equations.justification: Direct formalization of the abstract sentence; phase function phi and uniform amplitudes are assumed.
assumptions: phi is an unspecified monotone function

equations.label: Most probable path objective
equations.description: The Viterbi goal: the maximum-likelihood path.
equations.abstract_quote: the most probable path has a high probability of being measured
equations.justification: Target of amplification stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Number of legal paths
equations.description: Count of trellis paths for Q start states and fanout F over N steps (approximate, background).
equations.justification: Standard trellis counting; consistent with performance depending on fanout F rather than Q.
assumptions: Each state has exactly F outgoing transitions

registers.name: path
registers.size: N registers of ceil(log2 F) qubits each, plus start-state register of ceil(log2 Q) qubits (assumed encoding)
registers.role: encodes a legal path as start state plus a branch choice per frame

registers.name: phase/metric ancilla
registers.role: holds the path metric used to impose phase phi(P(pi|r)); uncomputed afterwards

specification.initial_state: All-zero registers; assumed encoding of a path as start state plus N branch choices.

steps.description: Prepare a uniform superposition over legal paths using the tensor-product (butterfly-like) structure, e.g. Hadamard-type gates on the start-state and branch registers.
Compute the path metric from received data r into an ancilla, apply a phase phi(P(pi|r)), and uncompute the ancilla to obtain |Psi>.
Apply the specialized amplitude amplification (oracle details unspecified in the abstract) one or more times to boost the amplitude of the maximum-probability path.

specification.measurement: Measure the path registers (start state and branch choices) in the computational basis after amplitude amplification; the outcome is the candidate most probable path pi*, with high probability if amplification succeeds.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Decode the measured bits into the state sequence and the corresponding information bits. Optionally compute P(pi|r) classically to check the candidate and repeat the run if it is not satisfactory.
assumptions: Path register encoding assumed as start state plus branch choices
Computational-basis measurement of path registers assumed
Optional classical verification and repetition assumed
missing_information: Amplitude amplification oracle and iteration count
Success probability and number of repetitions
